title: VAE and GAN model ideas
goal: Explain how reconstruction differs from adversarial generation.
case: A designer wants new simple icons similar to examples, without copying an exact icon.
terms: An encoder predicts the centre (μ) and spread (σ) of a small latent distribution. We sample a code z from it. A decoder uses z to reconstruct the image.
Nearby latent values often produce related outputs, though this is learned rather than guaranteed.
A generator proposes samples. A discriminator learns to distinguish generated and real samples; both change during training.
A lower loss alone does not certify useful images; inspect quality, diversity and a held-out sample.
steps: Trace an example through encoder, sample and decoder
Trace random input through generator and discriminator
Inspect supplied loss and quality figures
Change one latent coordinate in a toy visualization
example: Latent coordinate z changes from 0.3 to 0.7.
Toy decoder output changes; inspect rather than assume improvement.
misconception: The toy decoder is a trained VAE or a trained GAN.
correction: It is only a deterministic illustration of latent variation. Real models learn parameters from examples.
change: Change z and compare output difference; explain that the toy cannot establish realism.
metric: Mean absolute reconstruction error on supplied example pairs
lab: Annotate model paths and explore a toy latent coordinate.
output: Two labelled model diagrams and a reconstruction comparison.
